messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: DSM Prediction grid
parts:
Gareth:

If your study area is large, the portion of the study area around the
perimeter that does not fall into the prediction grid cell squares will
be small; and the approximation for the purposes of estimating abundance
will be adequate.

We have not worked with prediction grid cells that (by and large) are
not square. I suppose you could use some sort of tessellation but that
will make it more difficult to organise your covariate values. As a
rule the covariate data we have used for DSM analyses come to use from
remotely sensed data that are squares. All said and done, your life
will be simplest if you use your first option.

On to your next question: 'can I speed variance estimation
calculations' the simple answer is no. Bootstrap calculations are by
definition computationally expensive. You'll not speed the calculations
appreciably by moving your analysis directly into R. Your strategy of
making your segments as small as possible will cost you computing time,
as you have found. You might consider increasing your segment lengths
to bring down your computing burden. Model results tend to be (fairly)
robust to choice of segment size. Consider the scale of the covariates
you wish to use when debating the size of your segments.
